messages:
alex.k: hey — seeing a weird pattern in prod: tenant-42 started getting abuse-fallbacks even though their traffic looks normal. digging in logs now

maria.g: what kind of fallback? rate-limit? soft-shed?

alex.k: soft-shed at admission + abuse-score spike. root cause looks like KV-cache lease mismatch: two frontends had different lease-views for the same prefix, so requests were double-counted into the abuse window.

jin.lee: ouch. do you mean the lease was refreshed on A but B still thought it had ownership and admitted requests?

alex.k: exactly. sequence: A relinquishes, B hasn't updated, B serves, but the admission service sees both as valid holders -> duplicate credit accounting.

samr: is this specific to cross-zone failover or just transient lease races?

alex.k: mostly cross-zone timing + slow lease invalidation when the lease store had a txn stall. not common but enough to trip fairness for a small tenant.

maria.g: can we add a cheap affinity check at admission: verify current lease-holder from lease-store before counting credits?

jin.lee: yes but needs to be super cheap. admission path is hot. maybe a best-effort check with an eventual consistency fast-path: check local cache first, and only hit lease-store on mismatch or >X requests/s.

samr: also consider attaching lease-generation-id to requests from frontends. admission can reject if generation doesn't match the authoritative one. cheap compare in header.

alex.k: we already have lease-gen in metadata for internal RPCs but it's not propagated end-to-end. good idea to thread it.

maria.g: telemetry: we should emit metric when admission sees lease-gen mismatch vs when it hits the store. that helps tune the fast-path threshold.

jin.lee: actionables: 1) frontend: start attaching lease-gen header (opt-in flag) 2) admission: fast-path local compare + on-mismatch check store + metric 3) add one-off migration to reconcile caches after zone failover.

samr: add unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent lease handoff and ensure accounting only counted once.

alex.k: i'll draft a small follow-up RFC for the runtime side changes. quick sketch of the admission check:

```
# pseudocode
if req.lease_gen == local_cache[tenant].lease_gen:
  accept_counting()
else:
  if rate(req) < THRESHOLD:
    store_gen = lease_store.get(tenant)
    if store_gen == req.lease_gen:
      accept_counting()
    else:
      reject_or_route_fallback()
  else:
    reject_or_route_fallback()
```

maria.g: that looks fine. THRESHOLD should scale with per-tenant QPS. default tiny for small tenants.

jin.lee: also flag for rollout: start with only telemetry (no rejects) for 24h to measure false positives.

samr: and we should consider a reconciliation job that scans lease-store vs frontend caches and force-evicts stale caches post-failover.

alex.k: agreed. i'll open the RFC + a telemetry PR. mysql of logs attached in thread: `logs/prod/1769009852/kv-lease-events` (linked).

maria.g: perfect. tagging infra-oncall FYI: @deploy-bot can you run a canary when we have PR? :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: noted — will queue a canary deploy and report status in this thread once the admission PR is merged.

alex.k: timeline: RFC today, proto PR by EOD, telemetry-only rollout first, then conditional reject after 48h if metrics look clean.

jin.lee: +1. add a short playbook for rollback if we see spike in rejected customer requests.

samr: I'll take tests + reconciliation job.

alex.k: thanks all — will ping again when RFC link is up.
